paragraphs: Children in care in Halton, across Widnes and Runcorn, are looked after by foster carers approved through Halton Borough Council's own fostering service and by independent providers, including the agencies shown above. The council recruits carers through Foster4, a partnership it shares with Cheshire West and Chester and Warrington councils, and enquiries about fostering for the council go through that hub.

The council has been open about wanting more local carers. In May 2026 its newsroom said Halton needs foster carers and welcomed people from all backgrounds, including single people, couples, renters, homeowners and LGBTQ+ applicants, as long as they are 21 or over and can offer a safe, supportive home. Its placement sufficiency strategy set out an aim for most Halton children to live within the borough or close to it, and named sibling groups, disabled children and teenagers as priorities when recruiting carers.

The council's fostering statement of purpose describes the help carers can expect: a supervising social worker for each household, a mentor for newly approved carers, regular training, support groups, an out-of-hours duty team and help with essential items such as beds and car seats. It refers to financial support set out in separate allowance guidance rather than giving figures, so it is worth asking the council directly about current payments.

If you are thinking about fostering in Halton, a sensible first step is to request information from the council's service and from two or three of the services on this page. Comparing the training, support and payments each one describes will help you decide who to apply with.
